I'm 70 this year, and I've been farming these 18 mu for 50 years. My husband passed away some years back, but I still manage the farm with help from my sons and daughters-in-law. Two of my children work at a factory in town and send money home, which helps with input costs. There are 7 of us in the household including grandchildren, so we can't afford big risks.

I keep 10 mu in cotton and 8 mu in wheat-maize rotation. The cotton brings the most cash when prices are decent, but it's backbreaking work with all the picking — my daughter-in-law and I do most of it. The wheat-maize is our stable food and some income. We eat the wheat flour and sell the maize.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10th, after National Day. I buy the improved seed from the village supply shop — not the fanciest kind, but the one I've used for years that doesn't fail. Before planting, I spread about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu and plow it in. At green-up or jointing, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I'll spread another 20-30 jin of urea. I irrigate twice if the winter is dry — once before freeze-up and once at jointing. Pumping water from the well costs electricity money, so I don't over-water. I expect about 800 jin per mu if spring weather is normal.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, usually around June 12th to 15th. We only have about a week, sometimes less. I hire the neighbor's tractor to do quick rotary tillage, then we plant by hand or with the small machine. I use hybrid maize seed — it's 50 yuan per mu but worth it. I put fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 70 jin of compound per mu, and if it rains well I'll add some urea at the big trumpet stage. One irrigation in summer is usually enough — last year I didn't irrigate at all and still got decent yield because of the rain. I hope for 900 jin per mu.

For cotton, I plant in mid-April, around the 15th. I prepare the beds in early April and lay down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, half at planting and half when the plants flower. I irrigate twice — at flowering and when the bolls are forming. Cotton needs more pesticide than grain. I spray for weeds twice and for bollworms three or four times. The insecticide is expensive, maybe 60-70 yuan per mu total, but if you skip it the bollworms will eat everything. Picking starts in September and goes through October, three or four rounds. It's all family labor — we can't afford hired pickers at 150 yuan per day. I expect about 450 jin of seed cotton per mu, maybe 500 if the weather is kind.

All together, I'm spending about 6,800 yuan on seeds, fertilizer, water, and chemicals this year. That's a lot for us, but my son sent 5,000 yuan from his factory job last month, so we can manage. I don't hire much labor besides the tractor — family does the rest. At my age, I move slower than I used to, but I know every piece of this land.
